statuses.title: b-min-sep warm-start likelihood ratio misnormalizes the stationary mixture
statuses.note: 9df5a8dc rewrote likelihood_ratio_warm into a log-space WarmLogLikelihoodRatio. packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:102-106 now computes `log_numerator = log_add(log_f[0], log_p + log_sumexp(&log_f[1..bands]))` then `log_numerator - self.log_denominator` with `log_denominator = ln(1+(bands-1)p)` (:71) -- i.e. (f[0] + p*tail)/denom, the parenthesisation OPQ-300 asked for. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, not against the repo's own oracle: I re-implemented (a) the warm-start participation law by exhaustive enumeration over initial barred states x all 2^n masks and (b) the shipped DP, in Python (scratchpad/vfy_opq300.py). Shipped DP == exact enumeration to <=1e-15 relative over 6 cases (bands 1..5, n 3..10, p 0.17/0.5/0.999/1.0, sigma^2 0.81..2.0); the pre-fix formula overstated by 1.14x-1.71x on the same cases. The repo's pinned constant `privacy_loss_matches_jax_reference` (0.8329398380809252) equals my exact enumeration's ln bit-for-bit. End-to-end: bands=1 MC delta dominates `poisson_pld(gaussian_pld(sigma)).self_compose(n)` at every eps in {0,.25,.5,1,2,4} for (n,p,sigma) in {(8,.15,1.2),(20,.1,1.0),(50,.05,0.8)}. PERF REWRITE CHECKED: d0257cbf only hoists the evaluator into `for_each_init` state; the evaluator's only state is the `log_f` scratch, which is `resize`d to n+bands, has [n..] refilled with 0 and [0..n] fully rewritten on every call (mc.rs:81-101), so reuse across samples cannot leak state. Sibling check: the balls-in-bins MC ratio (balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:84-97) is the correctly 1/b-normalised mixture log-ratio and has no analogous defect. cargo test --workspace --lib: 397 passed / 0 failed.

statuses.title: b-min-sep Monte Carlo transcripts sharded by the live Rayon thread count
statuses.note: 6e3a7d03 ported the balls-in-bins scheme: `rayon::current_num_threads()` is gone from the whole crate (grep: only occurrences left are `ThreadPoolBuilder::num_threads` inside tests), both drivers now use fixed 1024-sample shards -- `par_chunks_mut(SAMPLES_PER_SHARD)` in bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld (mc.rs:382,411) and `par_chunks_mut(shard_cells)` in bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts (mc.rs:243,268) -- seeded by `shard_seed(seed, shard, direction)` (mc.rs:34-37), and the `+1000` direction offset is replaced by an even/odd split. REPRODUCED END TO END against a fresh `cargo build --release --features python-extension` of 12146ec4: coef [sqrt .7, sqrt .3], n=50, p=.05, sigma=1, seed=173, mc_resolution 5e-3, mc_fp 1e-2 gives epsilon_at(1e-2) = 1.7307448580168208 bit-identical at RAYON_NUM_THREADS = 1, 2, 3, 8, 16 and unset (the pre-fix build gives 1.8422 at 1 worker vs 1.8267 at 4). Rust identity tests (transcripts_are_identical_across_thread_counts, transcript_evaluation_is_identical_across_thread_counts, mc_pld_is_identical_across_thread_counts) plus a Python subprocess test (packages/opaque-accounting/tests/test_b_min_sep_reproducible.py) now cover both entry points; the Python transcript cache key includes seed and num_mc_samples (_transcript_cache.py:31). `samples_to_pmf` sorts with `par_sort_unstable_by(f64::total_cmp)` so the histogram stage is order-independent too. CAVEAT (filed as a finding): the ported `seed + 2*shard + direction` scheme makes seeds S and S+2 share every shard but one, so varying the seed by a small stride does not give an independent Monte Carlo replicate.

statuses.title: random_allocation.rs docstring claims discretisation error does not accumulate
statuses.note: 0cb6b7b7 replaced the false claim. packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs:13-18 now reads "The grid size does not grow across them, which makes large `t` tractable. Each pairwise convolution contributes at most `alpha` of privacy-loss discretisation error, so the total error for a `t`-fold convolution is bounded by `(floor(log2 t) + popcount(t) - 1) * alpha`." I checked the stated count against the implementation: `GeomPmf::self_conv` (pld/pmf/geom.rs:316-336) is binary exponentiation -- floor(log2 t) squarings (`base = base.conv(&base, dir)` guarded by `rem > 0`) plus popcount(t) accumulator merges of which the first is a `clone()` rather than a `conv`, i.e. exactly floor(log2 t) + popcount(t) - 1 convolutions, each rounding up one geometric grid step (`Rounding::Up`, error <= alpha in log-value, multiplicative errors compose additively in log space). `alpha` is a named field of the module's `Accuracy` struct (:36-47), so the symbol resolves. Docs-only change; per AGENTS.md test design guidance no verbatim-prose test is expected, and the pre-existing `test_larger_max_conv_grid_tightens_bound` still encodes the grid dependence.

statuses.title: self-convolution exponent silently truncated to u32 on the budgeted circular path
statuses.note: e858a470 added the boundary guard. packages/opaque-accounting/src/numerics/fft.rs:295-300 rejects `count > u32::MAX as usize` with InvalidParameter, and it sits after the singleton short-circuit (:288, which uses `pow_usize` and keeps full usize range) and strictly before the only `powu(count as u32)` site (:331). Grepped the whole crate for `as u32` / `powu`: the only other `as u32` casts are `(raw_ratio.log2().ceil() as u32).max(1)` in discretization/config.rs:219 and pld/pmf/dense.rs:458, which saturate to 0 on negative/NaN and are then clamped to >=1, so no second truncation site survives. Both entry points are covered because `self_convolve` (:161-162) delegates to `self_convolve_with_bounds`. Regression tests `test_fft_self_convolution_rejects_count_above_u32_max` and `test_circular_self_convolution_accepts_count_at_u32_max` exercise exactly the reproducer from the OPQ entry (`&[0.5,0.5]`, count = u32::MAX+1, Some((0,15)), allow_circular=true); both pass. Python boundary at python/pld.rs:36 still raises OverflowError above u32::MAX, so the two boundaries now agree.

statuses.title: asymmetric PLD beta metrics renormalize negative_infinity_mass away
statuses.note: e67927d7 resolved the inconsistency in the direction the symmetric path already used. `clean_probs` now takes negative_infinity_mass and renormalises to `1 - infinity_mass - negative_infinity_mass` (pld/metrics.rs:127-141); `pmf_beta_asymmetric` anchors the -inf atoms explicitly -- `cdf_y[0] = pmf_remove.negative_infinity_mass + probs_y[0]` (:317) and `cdf_add[0] = pmf_add.negative_infinity_mass + probs_x_add[0]` (:325, which is X = -L_add's +inf atom and so belongs in every ccdf_x entry); `pmf_beta_symmetrized` seeds `alpha_bar = pmf_add.negative_infinity_mass` (:427) and `f_alpha_bar = pmf_remove.negative_infinity_mass` (:435). I re-derived the new regression test's expected value from first principles rather than trusting it: for remove = {0.3 at -inf, 0.7 at loss 0} and add = {1.0 at loss 0}, the randomised Neyman-Pearson test at alpha=0.5 rejects the single finite atom with probability 0.5, giving beta = 0.3 + 0.5*0.7 = 0.65 -- exactly what `test_beta_asymmetric_includes_negative_infinity_mass` asserts, and 0.5 (wrong) under the pre-fix renormalisation. The same commit also repairs a latent negative-to-usize wrap: `((-x0 + 1).max(0) as usize)` / `((-y0 + 1).max(0) as usize)` (:425, :433) -- previously a negative intermediate wrapped to a huge usize and was clamped by `.min(n)`, silently returning Pr[X>0]=0 when the whole add PMF sat at loss index <= -2 and Pr[Y<=0]=full mass when the whole remove PMF sat at loss index >= 2. ε is untouched (`pmf_delta`/`pmf_epsilon` read only infinity_mass), matching the OPQ entry's eps:no. 397 lib tests pass.

findings.title: Monte Carlo shard seeds alias across nearby user seeds: seeds S and S+2 share all but one shard of the transcript corpus
findings.claim: The shard-seeding scheme introduced by the OPQ-301 fix (6e3a7d03) derives every per-shard RNG seed as `seed.wrapping_add((shard as u64).wrapping_mul(2)).wrapping_add(direction as u64)` -- i.e. the flat sequence seed, seed+1, seed+2, ... over (shard, direction) pairs. It is unique within one run (the crate test `shard_seeds_separate_adjacency_directions` only checks that), but it is not domain-separated across runs: `shard_seed(S, k, Remove) == shard_seed(S+2, k-1, Remove)` and `shard_seed(S, k, Add) == shard_seed(S+2, k-1, Add)` for every k >= 1. With the default discretization config, `resolved_num_mc_samples(2)` is 2_940_252 = 2872 shards of 1024, so a run at seed S and a run at seed S+2 draw 2871 of 2872 identical shards in each direction. Since `samples_to_pmf` is a pure function of the (sorted) sample multiset, the two runs are not independent Monte Carlo replicates -- they are the same estimate with one shard swapped. The scheme was copied verbatim from `balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:50-55` (the closed #331 fix), so both MC accountants -- b-min-sep, the auto sampler for BandMF, and balls-in-bins, the auto sampler for the correlated-noise MF mechanisms -- carry it.
findings.failure_scenario: A user wants to know how much of their reported BandMF epsilon is Monte Carlo noise, so they rerun the accountant at seeds 1000, 1002, 1004, ... and see a tight cluster, concluding the bound is stable. Measured through a fresh build of 12146ec4 (coef [sqrt .7, sqrt .3], n_steps=40, p=0.05, sigma=1.0, mc_resolution=1e-3, mc_failure_probability=1e-3 -> 17354 samples = 17 shards): seeds 1000,1002,1004,1006,1008,1010 give epsilon_at(1e-2) = 1.20193276, 1.20075917, 1.20075735, 1.21128410, 1.20904665, 1.21426936 (stdev 0.0059), while seeds 1000,2000,...,6000 give 1.20193276, 1.23670628, 1.21629628, 1.18018413, 1.22964362, 1.22441048 (stdev 0.0208). The stride-2 spread is 3.5x too small, matching the sqrt(2/17)=0.34 predicted by sharing 16 of 17 shards. At the default config the sharing is 2871/2872 and the stride-2 seeds are effectively indistinguishable. This does not invalidate any individual run -- each still carries its own simultaneous KL confidence band -- but it silently defeats seed variation as a stability check and makes an apparently reproduced (epsilon, delta, seed) triple less independent evidence than it looks.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:34-37 -- `fn shard_seed(seed: u64, shard: usize, direction: AdjacencyDirection) -> u64 { seed.wrapping_add((shard as u64).wrapping_mul(2)).wrapping_add(direction as u64) }`; introduced by 6e3a7d03 (#902).
packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:50-55 -- identical arithmetic, the sibling path the fix was ported from (closed #331).
packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:710-721 -- `shard_seeds_separate_adjacency_directions` only asserts within-run uniqueness, so no test can see the cross-seed aliasing.

packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:314 -- `samples.par_sort_unstable_by(f64::total_cmp)` in `samples_to_pmf`: the PMF depends only on the sample multiset, so shared shards propagate directly into the reported epsilon.

Measured with a release build of 12146ec4 (`cargo build --release --features python-extension`) driven from Python: stride-2 seed stdev 0.00594 vs stride-1000 seed stdev 0.0208 at 17 shards (script at scratchpad/, numbers quoted in the failure scenario).

packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.pyi:166 documents `seed` only as "RNG seed for reproducibility across worker counts within a fixed build" -- it makes no independence claim, which is why this is low rather than medium.
findings.fix_sketch: Hash the (seed, shard, direction) triple instead of adding them: e.g. seed a SplitMix64/ChaCha stream from `splitmix64(seed ^ (0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 * (shard as u64)) ^ (direction_tag << 63))`, or simply `StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed).long_jump(shard)`-style stream separation, so that distinct user seeds produce disjoint shard streams. Apply it to both `b_min_sep/mc.rs::shard_seed` and `balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs::shard_seed` together (the two must stay consistent, and the balls-in-bins copy is the origin of the pattern). Add a test asserting that the shard-seed sets for seed S and seed S+1 / S+2 are disjoint, not merely that they are unique within one run. Note this changes the sample corpus for a fixed seed, so cached transcript corpora and any pinned golden epsilons need regenerating.

delta_reviewed:
Scope: the Rust crate in packages/opaque-accounting (plus the root and crate Cargo.toml) over 4b13d82..12146ec4. Reviewed all 22 commits that touch those paths: 12146ec4, 3e8d6db1, 65dc1287, e67927d7, d0257cbf, aa15e6ac, 6e3a7d03, 9df5a8dc, 87404a1b, 51a18563, 76fd4e3e, 4bfd0c16, 20dd47aa, 3b22a6af, e87a0c21, 43fc883d, 2ecc00a8, 4867feb1, e858a470, 0cb6b7b7, a8a9c369, 7b26f655 (several of these turn out to be Python-only and were confirmed as such from their diffstats). Files read in full or in the changed regions: amplification/{mod.rs, poisson.rs, random_allocation.rs, truncated_poisson.rs, parallel_poisson.rs, b_min_sep/{mc.rs, registry.rs}, balls_in_bins/{mod.rs, monte_carlo.rs}}, numerics/{fft.rs, truncation.rs, logspace.rs}, discretization/config.rs, mechanisms/gaussian.rs, matrix_factorization/{bisr.rs, gram_matrix.rs, sensitivity.rs}, pld/{mod.rs, metrics.rs, pmf/{dense.rs, geom.rs}}, python/{mod.rs, amplification.rs, matrix_factorization.rs, config.rs, pld.rs}, lib.rs.

Build/test: `cargo test --workspace --lib` = 397 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` = 13 warnings, all in test code. I built the PyO3 extension at 12146ec4 (`cargo build --release --features python-extension`) into a scratch tree and A/B'd it against the extension binary already present in the source tree, which was built 2026-08-27 (the 4b13d82 commit date), giving a genuine pre/post comparison at the Python surface.

Numerical work done (all as read-only scripts in the scratchpad, nothing in the repo was modified): (1) independent exact enumeration of the warm-start b-min-sep participation law and mixture density ratio, versus a Python re-implementation of the shipped DP -- agreement to 1e-15, pre-fix formula off by 1.14x-1.71x; (2) RAYON_NUM_THREADS sweep {1,2,3,8,16,unset} on bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld -- bit-identical; (3) closed-form single-step hockey-stick for the Poisson-subsampled Gaussian (both adjacencies) versus `poisson_pld(gaussian_pld(sigma), q)` over 384 (sigma, q, eps) points -- zero underestimates; (4) the same against `poisson_pld(gaussian_pld(sigma).self_compose(k), q)` (the new non-Gaussian-source general path) versus the closed form at sigma/sqrt(k) over 162 points -- zero underestimates; (5) `poisson_pld(eps_delta_pld(e0,d0), q)` versus an exact four-atom transform of the canonical (eps,delta) dominating pair over 400 points -- zero underestimates; (6) old-versus-new epsilon at delta=1e-5 for 48 (sigma, q, n) subsampled-Gaussian configurations -- the generalized transform is uniformly 0.00-0.03 % LOOSER than the removed closed-form `poisson_gaussian_pld`, never tighter; (7) bands=1 b-min-sep MC delta versus the analytic poisson^n composition at three realistic configurations -- dominates at every eps tested; (8) brute-force enumeration of min-sep participation patterns versus `bisr_sensitivity_squared` for signed/oscillating coefficients -- always an upper bound (exact when the effective column is non-negative non-increasing, up to 2.2x conservative for adversarial signs).

Specific delta items checked and cleared:
- 3b22a6af feat(accounting): generalize Poisson PLD amplification (#850). `poisson_gaussian_pld` is replaced by `poisson_pld(base, rate)` with a `gaussian_source` fast path (mechanisms/gaussian.rs:32-40, pld/mod.rs:171-178). `compose`/`self_compose` clear the tag (pld/mod.rs:500, :558), so only pristine `gaussian_pld` outputs take the shortcut. Conservativeness of `realization_source`'s repairs verified by inspection: missing mass goes to +inf (increases delta), the E[exp(-L)]<=1 repair moves finite mass to +inf (strictly increases the hockey stick at every eps), and the >1 excess trim is bounded by REALIZATION_MASS_TOLERANCE=1e-8 and prefers non-positive-loss atoms. No dangling `poisson_gaussian_pld` references remain anywhere (single grep hit is the negative assertion in packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_amplification.py:230). Only cosmetic issue found: the transform fails with `Numerical error: Poisson transform produced unordered finite support` for rate below roughly 1e-14 where the old closed form returned 0; that is fail-closed and far outside any realistic sampling rate, so not filed.
- 87404a1b refactor(accounting)!: remove horizon prefix accounting (#894). Rust removal is complete and coherent: `random_allocation_gaussian_prefix_pld`, `k_out_of_t_gaussian_prefix_pld`, `weighted_mix_pmfs`, `validate_prefix_params` and `GeomPmf::add_constant` are all gone together with their `pub use` re-exports (amplification/mod.rs:28-29), their pyfunction wrappers and their `m.add_function` registrations (python/mod.rs). `grep -rn prefix packages/opaque-accounting/src --include=*.rs` returns only unrelated uses (BISR prefix norms, Pmf trimming). No dead code and no compiler warnings.
- d0257cbf perf(accounting): reuse b-min-sep likelihood evaluators (#913) -- explicitly re-checked for reintroduction of both OPQ-300 and OPQ-301; it changes only `for_each_init` state plumbing and neither the formula nor the shard seeding.
- Rounding directions on the conservative-bound math: `alloc_remove` rounds Up throughout; `alloc_add` deliberately rounds the inner convolution Down because an upper bound on -ln(S) needs a lower bound on S, then rounds the final projection Up (random_allocation.rs:105-130) -- correct. `toeplitz_majorant_sensitivity_squared` uses a reverse-suffix-max of |c| (bisr.rs:249-257), which is both a pointwise majorant of |c| and non-increasing as the Toeplitz theorem requires, so the bound direction is sound; the k>1 block decomposition in `random_allocation_gaussian_pld` (permutation-invariance + joint convexity) is a valid upper bound as documented. The BISR |C| substitution (gram_matrix.rs:235-242, bisr.rs:160-171, 386-390) is the row-wise triangle inequality and gives a Gram of the form M'^T M' with M' = [sum_e |C[:, i+eb]|], so it stays PSD; e87a0c21 also converts `lambda_cgd_gram_matrix_lr` / `bisr_gram_matrix_lr` into fail-closed tombstones rather than leaving an unsupported LR-weighted Gram reachable, which is the right direction.
- numerics/fft.rs `select_self_convolution_strategy` was rewritten to PREFER the aliasing circular transform whenever a tail budget exists and the bounded transform is <= 1/4 of the alias-free one, not only as an over-size fallback. I checked this for soundness rather than assuming it: circular aliasing only folds mass that lies outside [lower, upper] back INTO the window, it never removes in-window mass, and delta_at is monotone non-decreasing in every bucket mass, so delta_circular >= delta_linear-truncated always; the same out-of-window mass is separately and conservatively charged to infinity_mass / negative_infinity_mass in Pmf::self_compose (pld/pmf/dense.rs:352-366), and `compute_self_convolve_bounds_asymmetric` skips the left (resp. right) truncation entirely when that budget is zero. A/B over self_compose n in {2,10,50,100,500,1000,5000} at sigma in {1,3} shows epsilon differences of at most 1.4e-9 absolute in both directions, i.e. FFT-length roundoff, and both builds sit the same ~1.7e-8 relative below the analytic Gaussian (a pre-existing discretisation artifact reproduced identically by the pre-delta binary, so not a regression). No finding.
- Also spot-checked and found clean: the b-min-sep transcript registry (registry.rs; handle validates coef and p, n_steps comes from the corpus, and the only creator is the Python cache whose key includes coef/n_steps/p/num_samples/seed), `samples_to_pmf`'s KL confidence band and its `infinity_mass <= mc_resolution` guard, the `DiscretizationConfig` seed/max_conv_grid doc edits (aa15e6ac, 6e3a7d03), and the release-profile `debug = 1` added by 65dc1287 for the macOS LINKEDIT issue.
